01 / 04

The languages I know best

Urdu and Punjabi are my native languages, and I speak Hindi fluently.

They form the most established part of my language background. I think of them differently from the languages I am still beginning: the starting point is familiarity, and the next question is how well I can express a particular idea.

The connection

I am interested in how meaning changes with the words someone chooses.

Read the deeper context+

Even in a familiar language, tone and context matter. An everyday explanation, a formal message, and a discussion about an unfamiliar subject each need different wording. Knowing a language well gives me a starting point, but attention to the person still matters.

02 / 04

A background with more than one language

Being a Pakistani student in Saudi Arabia puts several languages around my life and education.

Urdu, Punjabi, and Hindi sit alongside the English I use for schoolwork and public writing, and the Arabic I am developing in Riyadh. I enjoy the different perspectives that come with that background, including the way an idea can be expressed differently.

The connection

Speaking more than one language makes me interested in phrasing.

Read the deeper context+

A sentence can be accurate and still sound distant, or simple and still lose something important. I want to become better at finding wording that keeps the meaning and feels natural to the person reading or listening. That is a skill I can keep developing.

03 / 04

Choosing the right words

Familiarity is especially useful when I need to focus on an idea instead of searching for a word.

Still, a new subject brings its own vocabulary. Legal, technical, and academic discussions ask for more care than an everyday conversation, and I want to learn that vocabulary properly as my studies become more demanding.

The connection

For me, good communication begins with understanding what the other person needs.

Read the deeper context+

Sometimes that is a direct answer; sometimes it is a slower explanation with a little more context. I want to be comfortable changing the way I explain something while keeping the underlying meaning clear and accurate.

04 / 04

What I want to improve

Urdu, Punjabi, and Hindi are only part of my language background.

English and Arabic have a different place in my current setting, while French, German, and Korean are still at the beginning. I find it useful to recognise those different starting points, because each suggests a different kind of practice and patience.

The connection

I want to keep improving the quality of my communication across all of them.

Read the deeper context+

That means listening carefully, noticing when a phrase is unclear, and becoming more precise in my writing. The aim is not simply to know another language name; it is to understand someone better and make my own meaning easier to follow.
